title: Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle via Cauchy-Schwarz
description: Robertson's 1929 generalization of the Heisenberg uncertainty principle: for any two self-adjoint operators A, B on a complex Hilbert space and any vector u, the product ‖Au‖·‖Bu‖ ≥ ½‖⟪(AB-BA)u, u⟫‖. Derived from Cauchy-Schwarz plus self-adjoint algebra.

overview.historicalContext: Heisenberg (1927) discovered the uncertainty principle relating position and momentum measurements in quantum mechanics. Robertson (1929) generalized this to any pair of self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space, showing the bound ‖Au‖·‖Bu‖ ≥ ½|⟨[A,B]u, u⟩| follows from abstract inner product geometry. The key algebraic insight is that self-adjoint operators make the commutator inner product ⟪(AB-BA)u, u⟫ equal to conj(⟪Au, Bu⟫) - ⟪Au, Bu⟫, a purely imaginary quantity whose norm is bounded by 2|⟪Au, Bu⟫|.
overview.problemStatement: For self-adjoint operators A, B on a complex Hilbert space E and any vector u ∈ E, prove ‖Au‖ · ‖Bu‖ ≥ ½‖⟪(AB-BA)u, u⟫_ℂ‖.
overview.text: The Robertson-Schrödinger uncertainty inequality states that for any self-adjoint A, B and any state u: ‖Au‖·‖Bu‖ ≥ ½|⟨[A,B]u,u⟩|. The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality ‖⟪Au, Bu⟫‖ ≤ ‖Au‖·‖Bu‖ is combined with the algebraic identity ⟪[A,B]u,u⟫ = conj(⟪Au,Bu⟫) - ⟪Au,Bu⟫ to give the bound.
overview.proofStrategy: Two steps: (1) Algebraic identity: for self-adjoint A, B, the self-adjointness property ⟪Ax,y⟫ = ⟪x,Ay⟫ implies ⟪ABu,u⟫ = ⟪Bu,Au⟫ = conj(⟪Au,Bu⟫) and ⟪BAu,u⟫ = ⟪Au,Bu⟫, so their difference is conj(z) - z where z = ⟪Au,Bu⟫. (2) Norm bound: ‖conj(z) - z‖ ≤ 2‖z‖ by triangle inequality, and ‖z‖ ≤ ‖Au‖·‖Bu‖ by Cauchy-Schwarz.
keyInsights: Self-adjointness of A makes ⟪Au, v⟫ = ⟪u, Av⟫, enabling the swap ⟪ABu, u⟫ = ⟪Bu, Au⟫
The commutator inner product ⟪(AB-BA)u, u⟫ = conj(⟪Au,Bu⟫) - ⟪Au,Bu⟫ is always purely imaginary

sections.title: Self-Adjoint Inner Product Symmetry
sections.summary: selfadj_inner: ⟪Ax, y⟫ = ⟪x, Ay⟫ for self-adjoint A. Uses A.adjoint = A and adjoint_inner_right.
sections.mathContext: For self-adjoint $A$ (i.e., $A^* = A$): $\langle Ax, y\rangle = \langle x, A^* y\rangle = \langle x, Ay\rangle$. This follows from the adjoint definition $\langle A^* y, x\rangle = \langle y, Ax\rangle$.

sections.title: Commutator Inner Product Identity
sections.summary: inner_commutator: ⟪(AB-BA)u, u⟫ = conj(⟪Au, Bu⟫) - ⟪Au, Bu⟫ for self-adjoint A, B.
sections.mathContext: Setting $z = \langle Au, Bu\rangle$: $\langle ABu, u\rangle = \langle Bu, Au\rangle = \overline{z}$ and $\langle BAu, u\rangle = \langle Au, Bu\rangle = z$. So $\langle [A,B]u, u\rangle = \bar{z} - z = -2i\,\mathrm{Im}(z)$, which is purely imaginary.

sections.title: Robertson-Schrödinger Uncertainty Inequality
sections.summary: heisenberg_norm_bound: ‖⟪[A,B]u,u⟫‖ ≤ 2‖Au‖·‖Bu‖. heisenberg_uncertainty: ‖Au‖·‖Bu‖ ≥ ½‖⟪[A,B]u,u⟫‖. heisenberg_uncertainty_commute: trivial when [A,B]=0. heisenberg_uncertainty_symm: symmetric in A,B. heisenberg_uncertainty_unit: form for unit vectors.
sections.mathContext: Chain: $\|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\| \leq 2\|\langle Au,Bu\rangle\| \leq 2\|Au\|\cdot\|Bu\|$ by the commutator identity + norm bound + Cauchy-Schwarz. Dividing by 2: $\|Au\|\cdot\|Bu\| \geq \frac{1}{2}\|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\|$.

conclusion.summary: The Robertson-Schrödinger uncertainty inequality is proved in 7 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. The proof reduces to Cauchy-Schwarz plus two elementary facts: self-adjoint symmetry and the norm of a conjugate difference.
conclusion.implications: The abstract form covers all quantum mechanical observables simultaneously. Setting A = position operator X and B = momentum operator P with [X,P] = iℏ gives the standard Heisenberg relation ΔX·ΔP ≥ ℏ/2.
openQuestions: Can the Schrödinger improvement ‖Au‖²·‖Bu‖² ≥ ¼|⟪[A,B]u,u⟫|² + ¼|⟪{A,B}u,u⟫ - 2⟪Au,u⟫⟪Bu,u⟫|² be formalized?
Can the equality condition (when the bound is achieved) be characterized in terms of eigenvectors of A + iλB?
